questions.q: The bouquet of roses ______ on the reception table.
questions.tip: Subject is 'bouquet', not 'roses'.

questions.q: Neither the coach nor the players ______ satisfied with the result.
questions.tip: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players'.

questions.q: By the time the ambulance arrived, the injured man ______ consciousness.
questions.tip: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

questions.q: My cousin ______ in Perth since she graduated.
questions.tip: 'Since' with an action continuing to now.

questions.q: Please switch off the lights ______ you leave the room.
questions.tip: A time relationship, not a contrast.

questions.q: There ______ hardly any milk left in the fridge.
questions.tip: 'Milk' is uncountable, so singular.

questions.q: The teacher asked us ______ during the assembly.
questions.tip: Reported command: told/asked + object + not to + verb.

questions.q: He is the only one of the prefects who ______ on duty today.
questions.tip: 'The only one' makes it singular.

questions.q: I would rather stay indoors ______ go out in this haze.
questions.tip: 'Would rather … than'.

questions.q: The twins helped ______ to the food at the buffet.
questions.tip: 'Theirselves' is not a word.

questions.q: ______ of the two answers is acceptable.
questions.tip: 'Either' is used for one of two.

questions.q: She apologised ______ her classmate ______ losing the book.
questions.tip: Apologise TO a person FOR a thing.

questions.q: The children were told to line up ______ the hall.
questions.tip: 'Outside' needs no extra preposition.

questions.q: If I ______ you, I would speak to the teacher immediately.
questions.tip: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons.

questions.q: Hardly ______ the bell rung when the pupils dashed out.
questions.tip: 'Hardly … when' requires inversion with 'had'.

questions.q: The stray dog, together with its puppies, ______ rescued yesterday.
questions.tip: 'Together with' does not change the subject.

questions.q: You ______ touch the wet paint; the sign says so clearly.
questions.tip: Prohibition, not absence of obligation.

questions.q: Nobody informed us about the change, ______?
questions.tip: 'Nobody' makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive.

questions.q: The results ______ announced next Monday.
questions.tip: Passive with a future modal: will be + past participle.

questions.q: I have ______ patience left after waiting for two hours.
questions.tip: 'Little' is negative and used with uncountable nouns.

questions.q: This is the shop ______ owner won the community award.
questions.tip: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: She speaks Malay far more ______ than her brother.
questions.tip: It describes the verb 'speaks', so an adverb.

questions.q: The soup smelt ______, so we finished every drop.
questions.tip: 'Smell' is a linking verb here, so an adjective follows.

questions.q: Ten kilometres ______ too far for a child to cycle.
questions.tip: A single distance is treated as one amount.

questions.q: He denied ______ the window.
questions.tip: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund.

questions.q: We are looking forward to ______ our grandparents next month.
questions.tip: 'Look forward to' + gerund; 'to' here is a preposition.

questions.q: ______ the heavy rain, the National Day rehearsal continued.
questions.tip: 'Despite' + noun phrase.

questions.q: The chairman, as well as the members, ______ present at the meeting.
questions.tip: 'As well as' does not add to the subject.

questions.q: I wish I ______ how to swim when I was younger.
questions.tip: A regret about the past takes the past perfect.

questions.q: That is the very book ______ I have been searching for.
questions.tip: After 'the very', 'that' is preferred.

questions.q: She is used to ______ up at five every morning.
questions.tip: 'Be used to' + gerund, unlike 'used to' + base verb.

questions.q: The number of dengue cases ______ fallen sharply this year.
questions.tip: 'The number' is a single thing.

questions.q: Not only ______ the race, but he also broke the record.
questions.tip: 'Not only' at the start of a clause forces inversion.

questions.q: My father insisted ______ paying for everyone's meal.
questions.tip: Insist ON.

questions.q: Please hand in your work ______ Friday at the latest.
questions.tip: 'By' means not later than.

questions.q: There were ______ people at the carnival than we expected.
questions.tip: People are countable.

questions.q: Neither of the twins ______ willing to admit fault.
questions.tip: 'Neither' is singular.

questions.q: The prize ______ by a Primary 4 pupil last year.
questions.tip: The prize receives the action, so passive.

questions.q: He ran ______ fast ______ nobody could catch him.
questions.tip: 'So + adverb/adjective + that'.

questions.q: It was ______ a moving speech that several parents wept.
questions.tip: 'Such + a + adjective + noun + that'.

questions.q: I have not seen him ______ we left primary school.
questions.tip: 'Since' + a point in time.

questions.q: The committee ______ divided over the proposal.
questions.tip: Here the members are acting as individuals, so plural.

questions.q: Let's begin the rehearsal now, ______?
questions.tip: 'Let's' always takes 'shall we'.

questions.q: She could not decide ______ to accept the offer.
questions.tip: 'Whether' is used before 'to + verb'.

questions.q: Every one of the exhibits ______ carefully labelled.
questions.tip: 'Every one' is singular.

questions.q: He behaved as if he ______ the owner of the place.
questions.tip: 'As if' with an unreal situation takes 'were'.

questions.q: The old bridge ______ down last month.
questions.tip: The bridge did not do the pulling.

questions.q: Rani plays the violin ______ than anyone else in the orchestra.
questions.tip: Comparing with 'than' needs the comparative.

questions.q: We had ______ finished lunch when the guests arrived.
questions.tip: 'Had just' shows the action was completed moments before.

questions.q: Do you know ______ the nearest MRT station is?
questions.tip: An embedded question keeps statement word order.

questions.q: The soup was very salty. Nobody could finish it. **(too)**
questions.m: The soup was too salty for anybody to finish
questions.tip: too + adjective + for + object + to + verb.

questions.q: He apologised. He had broken the vase. **(for)**
questions.m: He apologised for breaking the vase
questions.tip: Apologise for + gerund.

questions.q: She was very young. She could not understand the news. **(enough)**
questions.m: She was not old enough to understand the news
questions.tip: 'Enough' flips the adjective to its opposite.

questions.q: The film was boring. We left halfway. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The film was so boring that we left halfway

questions.q: "Have you finished your project?" the teacher asked me. **(Begin: The teacher asked …)**
questions.m: The teacher asked me whether I had finished my project
questions.tip: Yes/no question becomes 'whether' or 'if', with the tense shifted back.

questions.q: Someone will repair the lift tomorrow. **(Begin: The lift …)**
questions.m: The lift will be repaired tomorrow
questions.tip: Passive with a future modal.

questions.q: My uncle built this house. He is an architect. **(who)**
questions.m: My uncle, who is an architect, built this house
questions.tip: Non-defining clause takes commas.

questions.q: He did not study. He failed the test. **(Because)**
questions.m: Because he did not study, he failed the test

questions.q: He did not study. He failed the test. **(Because of)**
questions.m: Because of his lack of study, he failed the test
questions.tip: 'Because of' must be followed by a noun phrase.

questions.q: Rahim reached the station. The train had already left. **(By the time)**
questions.m: By the time Rahim reached the station, the train had already left

questions.q: "Please do not feed the animals," the keeper said. **(Begin: The keeper …)**
questions.m: The keeper asked us not to feed the animals
questions.tip: Negative request: asked + object + not to + verb.

questions.q: The pupils cleaned the classroom. The teacher praised them. **(Having)**
questions.m: Having cleaned the classroom, the pupils were praised by the teacher
questions.tip: 'Having + past participle' shows the earlier action.

questions.q: It began to rain. We immediately took shelter. **(As soon as)**
questions.m: As soon as it began to rain, we took shelter

questions.q: It began to rain. We immediately took shelter. **(No sooner)**
questions.m: No sooner had it begun to rain than we took shelter
questions.tip: Inversion, and 'than' not 'when'.

questions.q: She is a careful driver. **(carefully)**
questions.m: She drives carefully
questions.tip: Adjective + noun becomes verb + adverb.

questions.q: I have never eaten a spicier curry. **(Begin: This is the …)**
questions.m: This is the spiciest curry I have ever eaten

questions.q: He was late. He missed the opening ceremony. **(Consequently)**
questions.m: He was late; consequently, he missed the opening ceremony
questions.tip: A connector needs a semicolon or a new sentence, not a comma.

questions.q: Mother allowed me to go. I finished my homework first. **(only after)**
questions.m: Mother allowed me to go only after I had finished my homework

questions.q: The old lady could not climb the stairs. She was too weak. **(so … that)**
questions.m: The old lady was so weak that she could not climb the stairs

questions.q: Nobody in the choir sings as sweetly as Amirah. **(Begin: Amirah …)**
questions.m: Amirah sings the most sweetly in the choir
questions.tip: Also accept: Amirah sings more sweetly than anyone else in the choir.

questions.q: They cancelled the match. It was raining heavily. **(owing to)**
questions.m: The match was cancelled owing to the heavy rain
questions.tip: 'Owing to' + noun phrase.

questions.q: "I saw the accident yesterday," the witness said. **(Begin: The witness said …)**
questions.m: The witness said that he had seen the accident the day before
questions.tip: Simple past becomes past perfect; 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.q: You must submit the form. You will not be considered otherwise. **(Unless)**
questions.m: Unless you submit the form, you will not be considered

questions.q: The boy was rescued by a passer-by. He had fallen into the canal. **(who)**
questions.m: The boy who had fallen into the canal was rescued by a passer-by

questions.q: She practises daily. She has become an excellent pianist. **(By)**
questions.m: By practising daily, she has become an excellent pianist
questions.tip: 'By' + gerund.

questions.q: It is dangerous to cycle without a helmet. **(Begin: Cycling …)**
questions.m: Cycling without a helmet is dangerous
questions.tip: Gerund as subject.

questions.q: He left early. He wanted to avoid the crowd. **(in order to)**
questions.m: He left early in order to avoid the crowd

questions.q: The shop sells stationery. It also sells snacks. **(both … and)**
questions.m: The shop sells both stationery and snacks
questions.tip: Keep the two items parallel.

questions.q: My brother dislikes durian. I dislike durian too. **(neither)**
questions.m: Neither my brother nor I like durian
questions.tip: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'I'.

questions.q: He realised his error only when the results came out. **(It was not until)**
questions.m: It was not until the results came out that he realised his error

questions.q: The teacher explained the rule. We still did not understand. **(Even though)**
questions.m: Even though the teacher explained the rule, we still did not understand

questions.q: People believe that exercise improves memory. **(Begin: Exercise …)**
questions.m: Exercise is believed to improve memory
questions.tip: Impersonal passive.

questions.q: She started learning Mandarin three years ago. **(Begin: She has …)**
questions.m: She has been learning Mandarin for three years
questions.tip: 'For' + a length of time.

questions.q: The gate is locked. We cannot enter the field. **(prevents)**
questions.m: The locked gate prevents us from entering the field
questions.tip: Prevent + object + from + gerund.

questions.q: "Where did you buy this bag?" my friend asked. **(Begin: My friend asked …)**
questions.m: My friend asked where I had bought that bag
questions.tip: 'This' becomes 'that' in reported speech.

questions.q: He is too short to reach the top shelf. **(so … that)**
questions.m: He is so short that he cannot reach the top shelf

questions.q: The room was very untidy. It embarrassed my mother. **(such)**
questions.m: It was such an untidy room that my mother was embarrassed
questions.tip: such + a/an + adjective + noun + that.

questions.q: They have not repaired the escalator yet. **(Begin: The escalator …)**
questions.m: The escalator has not been repaired yet

questions.q: He was ill. He still attended the rehearsal. **(In spite of)**
questions.m: In spite of being ill, he still attended the rehearsal
questions.tip: Never write 'in spite'. Also accept: In spite of his illness.

questions.q: I prefer swimming to jogging. **(would rather)**
questions.m: I would rather swim than jog
questions.tip: 'Would rather' takes the base form of the verb.

questions.q: The referee blew the whistle. The players stopped at once. **(The moment)**
questions.m: The moment the referee blew the whistle, the players stopped

questions.q: She lost her wallet. It contained all her savings. **(which)**
questions.m: She lost her wallet, which contained all her savings
questions.tip: Non-defining clause: comma, and never 'that'.

questions.q: You should apologise. Then she may forgive you. **(If)**
questions.m: If you apologise, she may forgive you
questions.tip: No 'will' or 'should' in the if-clause.

questions.q: Everyone admired his courage. Nobody said so aloud. **(although)**
questions.m: Although everyone admired his courage, nobody said so aloud

questions.q: The hall was full. We had to stand at the back. **(As)**
questions.m: As the hall was full, we had to stand at the back
questions.tip: 'As' here means 'because'.

questions.q: My grandfather cannot read small print. His eyesight is poor. **(too)**
questions.m: My grandfather's eyesight is too poor for him to read small print

questions.q: He completed the marathon. Everyone was surprised. **(To everyone's surprise)**
questions.m: To everyone's surprise, he completed the marathon

questions.q: The librarian asked us to be quiet. We continued chatting. **(despite)**
questions.m: Despite the librarian's request for us to be quiet, we continued chatting
questions.tip: Also accept: Despite being asked to be quiet by the librarian, we continued chatting.

questions.q: Wei Ling is the tallest girl in the class. **(Begin: No other girl …)**
questions.m: No other girl in the class is as tall as Wei Ling

questions.q: "Let's organise a class party," said Ben. **(Begin: Ben suggested …)**
questions.m: Ben suggested organising a class party
questions.tip: Also accept: Ben suggested that we should organise a class party.

questions.q: Passage 3 — Last month, our class went on a excursion to the Botanic Gardens.
questions.m: an
questions.tip: The error was “a”. 'Excursion' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.q: Passage 3 — We were told to bring a cap, a water bottle and comfortable shoe.
questions.m: shoes
questions.tip: The error was “shoe”. Shoes come in pairs.

questions.q: Passage 3 — The bus journey took about fourty minutes.
questions.m: forty
questions.tip: The error was “fourty”. Spelling — 'forty' has no u.

questions.q: Passage 3 — Our guide, Mr Sim, were waiting for us at the entrance.
questions.m: was
questions.tip: The error was “were”. The subject is 'Mr Sim'.

questions.q: Passage 3 — He explain that the gardens were more than 160 years old.
questions.m: explained
questions.tip: The error was “explain”. The passage is in the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 3 — We saw many unusual plant along the rainforest trail.
questions.m: plants
questions.tip: The error was “plant”. 'Many' needs a plural noun.

questions.q: Passage 3 — My friend Nadia was fascinated by the orchids, which she photographed carefuly.
questions.m: carefully
questions.tip: The error was “carefuly”. Spelling — double l.

questions.q: Passage 3 — Suddenly, it started to rain, so we ran towards to the shelter.
questions.m: towards (delete 'to')
questions.tip: The error was “towards to”. 'Towards' already contains the direction.

questions.q: Passage 3 — By the time the rain stopped, our clothes was completely soaked.
questions.m: were
questions.tip: The error was “was”. 'Clothes' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 3 — Although we were wet, we enjoy the trip thoroughly.
questions.m: enjoyed
questions.tip: The error was “enjoy”. The passage is in the past tense.

questions.q: Passage 4 — My grandmother have lived in the same flat for over thirty years.
questions.m: has
questions.tip: The error was “have”. Singular subject.

questions.q: Passage 4 — Every Sunday, my family and me visit her for lunch.
questions.m: I
questions.tip: The error was “me”. It is part of the subject.

questions.q: Passage 4 — She always prepare her famous curry puffs in advance.
questions.m: prepares
questions.tip: The error was “prepare”. Third person singular.

questions.q: Passage 4 — The delicious smell greets us the moment we enter the kitchen.
questions.m: greets
questions.tip: No error of tense here — the error is the missing comma? In fact this line is correct as written; accept 'no error'.

questions.q: Passage 4 — Last week, she teached me how to fold the pastry properly.
questions.m: taught
questions.tip: The error was “teached”. 'Teach' is irregular.

questions.q: Passage 4 — I was very please when my first one turned out neatly.
questions.m: pleased
questions.tip: The error was “please”. It describes how I felt.

questions.q: Passage 4 — My younger cousin, who is only six, ate three of them by herself.
questions.m: herself
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 4 — Grandmother said that she would teach me her recipe for laksa nex time.
questions.m: next
questions.tip: The error was “nex”. Spelling.

questions.q: Passage 4 — I am looking forward to learn it from her.
questions.m: learning
questions.tip: The error was “learn”. 'Look forward to' takes a gerund.

questions.q: Passage 4 — These Sunday lunches is the happiest part of my week.
questions.m: are
questions.tip: The error was “is”. 'Lunches' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 5 — The annual sports day was hold at the national stadium this year.
questions.m: held
questions.tip: The error was “hold”. Passive needs the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 5 — Hundreds of pupils from six schools took part in the competition.
questions.m: took
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 5 — Our team had train hard for three months before the event.
questions.m: trained
questions.tip: The error was “train”. 'Had' needs the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 5 — The weather was humid, and many runners complained about the heat.
questions.m: about
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 5 — In the four hundred metres, Devi ran more faster than her opponents.
questions.m: faster
questions.tip: The error was “more faster”. Never double the comparative.

questions.q: Passage 5 — She won the race easy, finishing several seconds ahead.
questions.m: easily
questions.tip: The error was “easy”. It describes how she won.

questions.q: Passage 5 — Our relay team, however, were disqualified for a dropped baton.
questions.m: was
questions.tip: The error was “were”. The team acted as one unit.

questions.q: Passage 5 — We felt disappointed, but our coach reminded us that we had improve greatly.
questions.m: improved
questions.tip: The error was “improve”. 'Had' needs the past participle.

questions.q: Passage 5 — He said that perseverence was more important than medals.
questions.m: perseverance
questions.tip: The error was “perseverence”. Spelling — -ance.

questions.q: Passage 5 — On the bus home, we sang loudly and promised to train even harder nex year.
questions.m: next
questions.tip: The error was “nex”. Spelling.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Recycling is one of the easiest way to protect the environment.
questions.m: ways
questions.tip: The error was “way”. 'One of the' needs a plural noun.

questions.q: Passage 6 — In our estate, there is three large recycling bins at the void deck.
questions.m: are
questions.tip: The error was “is”. The verb agrees with 'bins'.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Unfortunately, many residents does not use them correctly.
questions.m: do
questions.tip: The error was “does”. 'Residents' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Food containers must be rinse before they are thrown in.
questions.m: rinsed
questions.tip: The error was “rinse”. Passive after 'must be'.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Otherwise, the whole batch of recyclables become contaminated.
questions.m: becomes
questions.tip: The error was “become”. The subject is 'batch'.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Our residents' committee has put up posters to explain the rules clearly.
questions.m: has
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 6 — Since than, the amount of contaminated waste has fallen sharply.
questions.m: then
questions.tip: The error was “than”. 'Then' refers to time.

questions.q: Passage 6 — My neighbour, Mr Rahman, collects old newspapers every Saturday morning.
questions.m: collects
questions.tip: This line is correct as written.

questions.q: Passage 6 — He says that small habits is what change a neighbourhood.
questions.m: are
questions.tip: The error was “is”. 'Habits' is plural.

questions.q: Passage 6 — I have decided to seperate my rubbish properly from now on.
questions.m: separate
questions.tip: The error was “seperate”. Spelling — there is 'a rat' in separate.

questions.q: The hikers were __________ by the sudden downpour and had to turn back.
questions.tip: Hampered = held back, obstructed.

questions.q: Her __________ handwriting made the letter a pleasure to read.
The boy gave a __________ excuse that nobody believed.
questions.tip: Feeble = weak.

questions.q: After the earthquake, volunteers worked to __________ the damaged homes.
The teacher's instructions were __________, so nobody was confused.
questions.tip: Explicit = stated very clearly.

questions.q: He accepted the award with a __________ smile and thanked his teammates.
The stray kitten looked so __________ that we took it to the vet immediately.
questions.tip: Frail = weak and delicate.

questions.q: Heavy traffic on the expressway __________ our arrival by an hour.
The audience listened in __________ silence as the pianist began.
questions.tip: Rapt = completely absorbed.

questions.q: She was __________ for her habit of arriving late to every meeting.
questions.tip: Notorious = famous for something bad.

questions.q: The evidence against him was __________; there was no room for doubt.
My grandfather has a __________ memory and can recall events from 1965.
The two brothers have __________ personalities; one is loud and one is quiet.
The manager __________ the customer's complaint and offered a refund.
Despite the setback, she remained __________ that the project would succeed.
The old warehouse was __________ and had not been used for decades.
questions.tip: Derelict = abandoned and in poor condition.

questions.q: He spoke so __________ that we could barely make out a single word.
The charity relies __________ on donations from the public.
questions.tip: Collocation: rely heavily on.

questions.q: Her __________ to finish the marathon impressed everyone at the finish line.
The path up the hill was steep and __________, so we walked in single file.
The chef __________ the sauce with a pinch of chilli.
After hours of negotiation, the two sides finally reached a __________.
The little girl clutched her doll __________ as the thunder rolled.
His __________ comment about her cooking upset her for days.
questions.tip: Offhand = casual and thoughtless.

questions.q: The museum houses an __________ collection of ancient pottery.
They set off at dawn to __________ the summit before nightfall.
The rumour spread __________ through the school within one recess.
He was secretly __________ of his younger sister's musical talent, and could not bring himself to congratulate her.
questions.tip: Envious = resentfully wanting what someone else has. The second half of the sentence rules the others out.

questions.q: The nurse spoke to the frightened child in a __________ tone.
The team's victory was __________; they had trailed by twenty points.
Please __________ from using mobile phones in the library.
questions.tip: Refrain from = hold back from.

questions.q: The instructions were so __________ that even a five-year-old could follow them.
A __________ of applause greeted the principal as she stepped onto the stage.
The company was fined for __________ the safety regulations.
After the argument, an awkward __________ fell over the dinner table.
He is a __________ reader and finishes two novels every week.
questions.tip: Voracious = extremely eager.

questions.q: The floodwater __________ slowly once the rain stopped.
questions.tip: Receded = moved back.

questions.q: Her explanation was __________ enough to satisfy even the strictest teacher.
The two witnesses gave __________ accounts, so the police were unsure whom to believe.
He apologised __________ and promised it would never happen again.

passages.text:
The Quiet Shop

Mr Habib's provision shop had stood at the corner of our block for as long as anyone could (1)______. It was narrow and dim, and the shelves reached so high that he kept a wooden stool behind the counter to (2)______ the tins on the top row. Nothing in it was arranged the way things are arranged in a supermarket. The sweets sat beside the batteries, and the rice was stacked in the (3)______ near the door.

When the new mini-mart opened across the road, everybody said Mr Habib would have to (4)______. The mini-mart was bright and air-conditioned, and its prices were lower. For a few weeks, his shop was almost (5)______. My mother, who had bought her cooking oil from him for eighteen years, admitted quietly that she had started going across the road instead, because it was (6)______.

But Mr Habib did not close. Slowly, the customers came (7)______. It was not because his prices changed; they did not. It was because he remembered things. He knew that Mrs Lim's grandson was (8)______ to eggs, and he would say so if she reached for the wrong packet. He kept a box of plasters under the counter for children who fell outside, and he never (9)______ anyone for them. When old Mr Chua could no longer manage the stairs, Mr Habib carried his groceries up to the fourth floor himself, twice a week, without ever being (10)______.

The mini-mart is still there. So is the shop. My mother buys her rice across the road, because it is cheaper, and her cooking oil from Mr Habib, because — as she puts it — some things are worth a few extra (11)______.

I understand her now, although I did not then. A shop sells you things. Mr Habib's shop also (12)______ that somebody in the neighbourhood knew your name, your family and your habits. That is not something a mini-mart can put on a (13)______.

He is seventy-three this year and shows no sign of (14)______. I hope he never does. When he finally closes those shutters for the last time, our block will lose something it cannot (15)______.

Learning to Fail

When I was eleven, I was selected for the school debating team. I had never lost an argument at home, and I (16)______ that debating would be much the same. My first competition cured me of that idea within four (17)______.

The opposing speaker was a girl from another school who could not have been taller than my shoulder. She spoke slowly, which I mistook for (18)______. Then she began taking apart my argument, point by point, using my own words against me. By the time she sat down, I could feel my ears (19)______. I had prepared for a fight and had instead been quietly dismantled.

We lost. On the bus home, I stared out of the window and refused to (20)______ to anyone. My coach, Mr Menon, sat down beside me and said nothing for several stops. Then he asked me what she had done well.

It was not the question I was (21)______. I wanted sympathy, or at least somebody to agree that the judges had been unfair. Instead I had to think. Reluctantly, I said that she had listened to me properly, and that she had answered what I had actually said rather than what she had (22)______ I would say.

"Good," he said. "Now you know what to (23)______."

Over the next two years I lost eleven more debates. I also won nineteen. But it is the losses I can still (24)______ in detail, because each of them taught me something specific: to slow down, to listen before replying, to (25)______ my own weakest point before my opponent found it.

I have noticed since that people who have never failed at anything are often strangely (26)______ of trying. They protect a record instead of building a (27)______. I was lucky. I failed early, in front of forty people, in a school hall that smelt of floor polish — and the world carried on exactly as (28)______.

Mr Menon retired last year. In his farewell speech he said that his job had never been to make his pupils win, but to make losing (29)______ enough that they would risk it again. I did not appreciate that at eleven. I am (30)______ for it now.

answers.tip: 'As long as anyone could remember' is a set phrase.
A stool is used to reach high shelves.
Must be a place.
The prediction is that the shop will not survive.
Customers had gone across the road.
Any reason consistent with the earlier description of the mini-mart.
'Came back' — they had left earlier.
